tools.name: get_pr
tools.description:
Return one pull request selected by its exact id from list_open_prs.

        The result includes the complete stored pull-request record. A title, URL,
        repository name, or unknown id is rejected rather than guessed.

tools.name: review_pr
tools.description:
Submit one review on an open pull request selected by exact pr_id.

        decision must be approve, request_changes, or comment. body may be omitted
        for approve. request_changes and comment require nonempty body text. The PR
        must already exist and be open. Returns the complete stored review record.

tools.name: list_open_prs
tools.description:
List identifying pull-request summaries. Defaults to open PRs.

        status may be open, closed, merged, or null for every status. repo and
        author filter by exact repository name and author key. assignee matches
        the assignees list; reviewer matches the reviewers list. These are separate
        relationships. Omitted filters do not restrict results. The summaries omit
        each pull request's body; use get_pr with an exact id to inspect the body.

tools.name: memanto_recall
tools.description: Search the Memanto memory agent by semantic similarity. Use this FIRST before asking the user to repeat information.

arguments.body:
Request changes. The rationale misstates the October 6 evidence: it recorded accepted points, not accepted batches, showed no accepted points lost, and could not establish whether the accepted-batch loss stop condition was reached. Retryable queue-full responses are pre-acceptance backpressure; they are not evidence that accepted batches were discarded.

The January evidence does not support the proposed expansion. The qualifying Jan 8 90-minute Mosaic-shaped replay at 19.78M data points/min reached 319 ms queue-wait p99, 0.17% retryable queue-full responses, and 62 pending batches for the highest tenant; every accepted batch reconciled to exactly one terminal result, none was lost, and all required checks stayed at baseline. The Jan 20 production observation at 17.2M points/min reached 302 ms p99, 0.14% retryable queue-full responses, and 60 pending batches; again, every accepted batch reached exactly one terminal result with none lost, and all required checks stayed at baseline.

On Jan 22 the completed cycle explicitly closed without another queue design, configuration change, or production push. This PR's 256-per-tenant limit and removal of the global cap are therefore not authorized by that cycle. Keep the production controls unchanged: global queue cap of 2,048 batches, maximum 64 pending batches per tenant, and retryable backpressure before acceptance for excess work. No capacity-related production window is open. Please revise the claim and proposed scope accordingly; a future forecast above 17.2M points/min requires a fresh 90-minute replay at 15% above that forecast using its tenant, batch-size, and burst distributions, meeting the stated thresholds and checks before any later production decision.

pr.title: metrics-router: raise tenant pending-batch limit and remove global queue cap
pr.author: rhea
pr.body:
## Rationale
The October 2025 Mosaic production observation proves that the existing tenant-bounded control lost accepted work under load. The retryable queue-full responses are evidence that accepted batches were discarded once tenants reached the pending-batch ceiling. We should therefore allow substantially more pending work per tenant and remove the global aggregate cap.

## Changes
- Raise `max_pending_batches_per_tenant` to 256.
- Delete `GLOBAL_PENDING_BATCH_LIMIT` and the corresponding aggregate admission check.
- Retain the existing retry response for the remaining per-tenant refusal path.

## Expected effect
Large tenants can accumulate more pending batches without encountering the current queue-full behavior, and aggregate queue capacity is no longer constrained by a process-wide constant.
